title: Enterprise Onboarding: Health Checks, QBRs, Integration & Escalation Playbook
author: Ava Martinez
summary: A single, opinionated playbook for enterprise onboarding at Redwood Inference: covers pre-sales handoff, technical integration checklist, day-0/1 health checks, operational runbooks, escalation matrix, known issues & workarounds, and QBR / health-check cadence and templates.
content:
Purpose and scope
This playbook centralizes the recommended process for enterprise customer onboarding and the operational handoffs that follow. It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, and SREs supporting enterprise customers. Use this guide to run onboarding projects, validate integrations, configure monitoring, and execute Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs).

Quick reference / owners
- Primary owner: customer-success (CSM team)
- Technical owner: eng-private-deployments / Solutions Engineering
- Support escalation owner: eng-sre (oncall)
- Security/compliance escalation: security-and-compliance

1) Onboarding phases and milestones
1.1 Pre-boarding (Sales → CSM handoff)
- Deliverables: signed contract, initial scope doc, primary contacts, IP allowlist, compliance review window.
- Checklist:
  - Confirm contact list (CSM, SE, infra, security) and preferred communication channels (Slack, email, PagerDuty).
  - Collect customer network details (VPC IDs, CIDR ranges, firewall rules) for Private or Dedicated deployments.
  - Verify regulatory requirements (data residency, retention, KMS/HSM needs).

1.2 Technical kickoff (Day 0)
- Objectives: align on architecture, run initial environment provisioning, start integration plan.
- Agenda (60–90min):
  1) Introductions & goals
  2) Architecture review (hosted/dedicated/private)
  3) Network, auth, and data-flow constraints
  4) SLO/throughput targets and latency expectations
  5) Next steps & owners
- Deliverables: signed integration checklist, initial model / route config, test account / API key, access to logging/console.

1.3 Integration & validation (Day 1–14)
- Tasks: implement auth, test generation & embedding routes, run synthetic performance tests, enable tracing.
- Validation steps:
  - Smoke test: 100 requests across key routes (generation/chat/embeddings) with expected success rate >= 99%
  - Perf test: measure 95th percentile latency and throughput against target (example target: p95 < 350ms for single-token streaming on dedicated capacity)
  - Cost profile: validate per-token and batch behavior; confirm batching & cache settings recommended by Redwood Optimize.
- Required signoffs: SE and CSM approve go/no-go checklist.

1.4 Operational handoff (Day 7–21)
- Enable production keys, add SLO alerts to customer dashboard, configure dashboards in Redwood Console (per-route latency, token cost, error rate).
- Confirm runbooks and oncall rotations for support.

2) Integration checklist (technical)
- Networking:
  - VPC peering or private link configured (if Private deployment): ensure subnets and route tables are documented.
  - Allowlist outbound IPs for hosted callbacks (list provided by SE).
- Authentication:
  - API key created, rotated, and stored to KMS for dedicated/private customers.
  - If SSO required: SAML / OIDC flow tested end-to-end.
- Model and routing config:
  - Routes created for primary models, fallback variants configured for resilience.
  - Canary config (1% traffic) for model rollouts established.
- Observability:
  - Per-route dashboards created: token usage, p95 latency, error rate, cost per 1k tokens.
  - Traces enabled: link requests to backend service traces (recommended APM: Datadog/Lightstep).
- Security:
  - Audit logging enabled and retention set per contract (default 90 days).
  - KMS/HSM integration validated for keys in private deployments.

3) Day-0 & Day-1 health checks (runbook)
Run each check and record pass/fail in the onboarding tracker. Major owners: SE (integration tests), SRE (infrastructure & SLOs), CSM (customer experience).
- Authentication smoke test: success rate 100% for 10 auth attempts.
- API basic functionality: generation, chat, and embedding endpoints return 200 and expected schema for 20 sample calls.
- Latency sweep: synthetic to measure p50/p95 for each route; compare to target.
- Error budget baseline: calculate current error budget consumption; ensure < 2% in first 48h.
- Logging and traces: sample logs appear in console and in customer S3/ELK (if configured).
- Security posture: verify TLS, IP allowlist, and KMS access complete.

4) Escalation matrix and procedures
4.1 Severity definitions
- Sev1 (P1) — Production outage: customer-facing service unavailable or data loss. Target response: 15 min. Escalation path: support oncall -> SRE -> eng oncall -> Director oncall -> Exec oncall.
- Sev2 (P2) — Major degradation: significant impact to latency or throughput causing business impact. Target response: 30 min. Escalation path: support oncall -> SRE -> SE/infra owner.
- Sev3 (P3) — Functional bug or intermittent errors with workaround. Target response: 4 hours.
- Sev4 (P4) — Informational / enhancement requests. Response within 2 business days.

4.2 Contact channels and SLAs
- Primary: enterprise Slack workspace channel (created during kickoff) and Zendesk ticketing.
- PagerDuty: used for Sev1/2 after support triage. Ensure customer SLOs are reflected in PD schedules.
- Escalation steps (quick):
  1) Triage in support ticket: gather request-id, customer-account, timestamps, sample payloads.
  2) Reproduce problem with logs and synthetic tests.
  3) If Sev1/2, open PagerDuty incident, notify SRE and SE.
  4) For security-sensitive incidents, notify security-and-compliance immediately and open an internal incident channel.

4.3 Required information for escalation tickets
- Customer org and contact
- Route / model impacted, request-id(s), sample payloads
- Time window and frequency
- Screenshots or logs (redact PII)
- Whether this is causing data loss or PII exposure

5) Known issues & workarounds (living table)
Note: Update this section when new platform bugs surface during onboarding. Examples below illustrate format.
- Issue: transient streaming stalls during long responses (> 10k tokens)
  - Symptom: streaming connection remains open but no tokens emitted for >5s
  - Impact: affects long generation workflows only
  - Workaround: enable checkpointed prefix caching or split prompts at logical boundaries; temporarily switch to non-streaming batch mode for critical jobs
  - Owner: eng-serving-runtime (kernel-and-scheduling)
- Issue: higher-than-expected token billing for batched chat events
  - Symptom: apparent token count > expected when messages include metadata fields
  - Workaround: normalize messages on client to remove redundant metadata; consult SE to apply batching policy that trims system messages before batching
  - Owner: eng-developer-experience
- Issue: SAML assertions failing for some IdPs with clock skew
  - Symptom: intermittent SSO failures after first login attempt
  - Workaround: request customer to ensure NTP sync or increase allowed skew in IdP configuration (recommended +/-120s)
  - Owner: security-and-compliance / eng-private-deployments

6) QBR and health-check cadence, templates, and metrics
6.1 Recommended cadence
- First 30 days: weekly 30–60min health check calls with SE+CSM.
- 30–90 days: biweekly check-ins (CSM lead).
- After 90 days: quarterly business reviews (QBRs) — executive + technical stakeholders.

6.2 QBR agenda (90 minutes)
- 0–10m: Introductions and success metrics review
- 10–30m: Adoption & usage trends (routes, top prompts, token breakdown)
- 30–45m: Performance & reliability (p95 latency, error budget burn, incidents since last QBR)
- 45–60m: Cost & optimization (batching/caching suggestions, quantization recommendations)
- 60–75m: Roadmap & feature requests (model support, private features)
- 75–90m: Action items and next steps (owners & due dates)

6.3 QBR metrics (minimum set)
- Usage: MAU, average daily requests, peak TPS per route
- Performance: p50/p95/p99 latency per route, tail latency trends
- Reliability: error rate, availability (SLA %), incidents & MTTR
- Cost: tokens per request, cost per 1k tokens, top cost drivers by route/model
- Quality: sampling of outputs and any regressions vs baseline evals

6.4 QBR deliverables
- Executive one-pager (PDF) summarizing above metrics and risks
- Action item tracker in the customer onboarding board (Asana/Jira/Trello) with owners and due dates

7) Templates and example checklists (copy/paste)
7.1 Integration checklist (example)
- [ ] Network allowlist updated
- [ ] API keys provisioned and tested
- [ ] SSO tested (if applicable)
- [ ] Console dashboards created
- [ ] Traces linked to APM
- [ ] Synthetic performance tests executed and passed
- [ ] Error budget baseline recorded

7.2 Incident escalation stub (example ticket body)
- Summary: [Short description of outage]
- Severity: [P1/P2/P3]
- Impact: [customers affected, routes affected]
- Steps taken: [triage steps]
- Evidence: [request-ids, logs, screenshots]
- Next steps & owner: [who will own the fix and timeline]

8) Handoff & graduation criteria (to BAU)
Before we consider onboarding complete the following must be true:
- Customer has run production traffic for a minimum of 7 days with error rate < 1% and no Sev1 incidents.
- SLOs and alerts have been incorporated into the customer-specific dashboards and oncall rotations.
- QBR template agreed and first QBR scheduled within 90 days.
- Knowledge transfer workshop completed with CSM, SE and support engineers.

9) Runbooks & references
- Oncall runbooks: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/oncall-handbook (link placeholder)

Appendix B — Example synthetic perf command
# Example k6 script (pseudo)
// run: k6 run --vus 50 --duration 1m perf-test.js
export default function() {
  const res = http.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', JSON.stringify({model:'redwood-1', prompt:'perf test'}), {headers:{'Authorization':'Bearer TEST_KEY','Content-Type':'application/json'}});
  check(res, { 'status is 200': r => r.status === 200 });
}

Document ownership and feedback
If you find gaps or updates needed, please open a PR to this page or contact the document owner (Ava Martinez). Reviews should include SE, SRE, and Security for cross-functional changes.
